name: Autochrome
desc: Colour made of dyed potato starch — millions of orange, green and violet grains sieved into a random mosaic with lampblack packed in the gaps, and because every grain is a little lens at its own angle the whole plate shimmers as it is turned to the lamp; offered as Lumière starch, Dufay's woven réseau, a Joly line screen, a plate whose dyes have died, or the bare screen with no picture behind it at all.

energy.doc: lamp gain — how hard the plate is lit and how much the screen emits

scale.doc: starch grain size: 0.3 is a fine invisible screen, 2.6 is coarse chunky pointillism

density.doc: how tightly the grains are packed — low leaves lampblack showing between them

fade.doc: dye deterioration — the colour dying back toward a fogged monochrome ghost

hue.doc: the first dye (32 = the classic orange-red); the other two sit at +108 and +240 off it

speed.doc: how briskly the plate is turned (the tilt shimmer keeps its own floor regardless)

alpha.doc: master opacity of the whole pass

style.doc: which colour screen is bonded to the plate — these differ in the structure that makes the image (a random starch mosaic, a woven square réseau, ruled lines, dead dyes, or the naked screen)

act.doc: multi-minute program: held steady under a wandering lamp, turned about in the hand, or the dyes dying away until a fresh plate is brought out
